title: Payment API Returns HTTP 500
description: A payment endpoint returns an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error during payment processing.
diagnostic_checks: Review application logs around the failed request and note any exception or correlation ID.
Check whether the payment service is healthy and review its recent error rate.
Verify database connectivity if logs indicate database-related failures.
Check the external payment gateway status and dependency timeouts.
Review recent deployments and configuration changes; compare failures before and after the change.
known_resolutions: Correct the underlying code or configuration issue after confirming it from logs.
Restore database connectivity if a database failure is confirmed.
Address the external gateway or timeout configuration if evidence points to that dependency.

title: Application Cannot Connect to Database
description: An application cannot establish a connection to its configured database.
diagnostic_checks: Capture the exact database error and timestamp from application logs.
Confirm the database service is running and reachable from the application host.
Verify the configured hostname, port, database name, and network route.
Check credentials and secret configuration without printing passwords into logs.
Inspect database connection limits and connection-pool usage.
known_resolutions: Correct an invalid host, port, or database name when confirmed.
Restore the database service or network access if unavailable.
Review connection-pool sizing and leaked connections if connection exhaustion is confirmed.

title: Users Unable to Log In
description: Users cannot authenticate to an application.
diagnostic_checks: Record the exact error code and determine whether one user or many users are affected.
Check identity-provider or authentication-service health.
Verify token expiry, clock synchronization, and authentication configuration where applicable.
Review authentication logs while avoiding collection of passwords or active tokens.
Check recent changes to identity-provider settings or login flows.
known_resolutions: Correct authentication configuration if a configuration mismatch is confirmed.
Restore the identity-provider integration if its service is unavailable.
Guide the user through the approved credential-reset process if the issue is account-specific.
escalation_team: Identity and Access Management / Application Support

title: API Returns HTTP 404
description: An API request returns Not Found because the requested resource or route cannot be found.
diagnostic_checks: Verify the request URL, HTTP method, path, and required path parameters.
Check the API documentation and deployed route definitions.
Confirm the request is being sent to the intended environment or base URL.
Review gateway or reverse-proxy routing rules if the application route appears correct.
Check whether the resource identifier exists, if the endpoint expects a specific resource.
known_resolutions: Correct the URL or HTTP method if it does not match the documented route.
Correct routing configuration if the gateway is directing requests incorrectly.
Use a valid resource identifier when the requested resource does not exist.

title: API Returns HTTP 401 or 403
description: An API request is rejected because authentication is missing or invalid, or access is not permitted.
diagnostic_checks: Check whether the request includes the required authentication mechanism.
Verify token expiry and issuer or audience configuration where applicable.
For HTTP 403, check the user's role, permissions, and access policy.
Review authentication and authorization logs without exposing secrets.
Compare the failing request with a known-good request using safe test credentials.
known_resolutions: Refresh or replace an expired credential through the approved process.
Correct missing permissions when the access policy confirms that access should be allowed.
Correct authentication configuration if issuer, audience, or related settings are wrong.
escalation_team: Identity and Access Management / API Engineering

title: Application Is Running Slowly
description: An application has unusually high response times or slow page and API operations.
diagnostic_checks: Identify which pages or endpoints are slow and record the time window.
Compare response-time metrics and request volume with a normal baseline.
Inspect application logs and traces for slow operations or dependency waits.
Check CPU, memory, thread pools, and database query latency.
Review recent deployments and configuration changes.
known_resolutions: Optimize a slow query or operation after profiling identifies it as a bottleneck.
Address resource saturation if metrics confirm CPU, memory, or thread-pool exhaustion.
Roll back a problematic change only through the approved deployment procedure and after evidence supports it.

title: Service Unavailable or HTTP 503
description: A service returns HTTP 503 or cannot serve requests temporarily.
diagnostic_checks: Check service health checks and recent availability alerts.
Determine whether the issue affects all users or a subset of requests.
Inspect deployment status, instance count, and load-balancer health.
Check resource saturation and dependency availability.
Review recent deployments or maintenance activity.
known_resolutions: Restore unhealthy service instances if health checks identify them as unavailable.
Resolve a confirmed dependency outage or resource-exhaustion condition.
Follow the approved rollback or recovery procedure if a recent change caused the outage.

title: Connection Timeout to a Remote Service
description: A client or application does not receive a response from a remote service before the timeout.
diagnostic_checks: Record the destination host, port, request time, and exact timeout error.
Check whether the destination service is healthy and reachable from the caller's environment.
Review DNS resolution, firewall rules, proxy settings, and network routes as applicable.
Compare connection timeout and read timeout metrics.
Check dependency latency and request volume before changing timeout settings.
known_resolutions: Restore network reachability if a network or firewall issue is confirmed.
Resolve the remote service's availability or performance issue if supported by monitoring.
Adjust timeout values only when justified by expected latency and service-level requirements.

title: DNS Name Resolution Failure
description: A system cannot resolve a hostname to an IP address.
diagnostic_checks: Verify the hostname spelling and environment-specific DNS name.
Test resolution using approved tools such as nslookup or dig.
Check the configured DNS resolver and whether other names resolve.
Determine whether the DNS record was recently changed or removed.
Compare resolution from the affected host with a known-good environment.
known_resolutions: Correct the hostname if it is misspelled.
Restore or correct the DNS record if the record is missing or incorrect.
Escalate resolver or network problems to the team responsible for DNS.

title: File Upload Is Failing
description: Users cannot upload files through an application.
diagnostic_checks: Capture the exact error code and test with a permitted small sample file.
Check configured file-size and allowed-file-type limits.
Review reverse-proxy and application request-size limits.
Check available storage and permissions on the upload destination.
Inspect application logs for timeout, validation, or storage errors.
known_resolutions: Use an allowed file type and remain within documented size limits.
Correct inconsistent request-size limits when authorized and appropriate.
Restore destination storage access if a permission or storage failure is confirmed.

title: Application Uses Excessive Memory
description: Application memory usage grows unusually high or the process is terminated due to memory pressure.
diagnostic_checks: Check memory metrics and identify whether usage is sustained or a short-lived spike.
Review application logs for out-of-memory errors and restart events.
Compare memory use with request volume and recent deployments.
Use approved profiling or heap-dump procedures if available and safe.
Check container or host memory limits before changing them.
known_resolutions: Fix a confirmed memory leak or excessive allocation.
Adjust memory limits only after validating capacity and application requirements.
Escalate recurring memory failures to the application engineering team.

title: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests
description: An API rejects requests because a configured rate limit has been exceeded.
diagnostic_checks: Check response headers and API documentation for rate-limit information.
Determine whether request volume increased or a retry loop is occurring.
Review rate-limit metrics and identify the affected client or endpoint.
Check whether the response includes a Retry-After value.
Inspect client retry behavior and ensure retries use backoff where appropriate.
known_resolutions: Reduce request frequency or batch requests when supported.
Implement appropriate backoff and honor Retry-After when provided.
Request a limit change through the service owner if the workload legitimately requires it.

title: Application Fails After a Deployment
description: Errors or service degradation begin after a software deployment or configuration change.
diagnostic_checks: Compare the incident start time with deployment and configuration-change records.
Review release logs, health checks, and error rates before and after the change.
Identify affected versions, instances, endpoints, and user groups.
Check migration compatibility and changed environment variables.
Follow the team's incident procedure before rollback or further changes.
known_resolutions: Correct the identified regression or configuration problem.
Use the approved rollback procedure when evidence links the incident to the release and rollback is safe.
Verify service health and error rates after remediation.

title: Application Returns HTTP 400
description: An API rejects a request as malformed or invalid.
diagnostic_checks: Inspect the response body for validation details.
Compare the request payload with the API schema and required fields.
Verify data types, content type, encoding, and parameter formats.
Check whether the client is using the correct API version.
Reproduce with a minimal safe test request.
known_resolutions: Correct the request format or required fields based on validation feedback.
Use the documented API version and content type.
Escalate if a schema-compliant request is rejected unexpectedly.

title: Background Job Is Not Processing
description: A scheduled or queued background task is delayed or not executing.
diagnostic_checks: Check queue depth, oldest message age, and job status.
Verify worker health and scheduler status.
Inspect job logs for repeated failures or poison messages.
Check dependency availability and worker resource usage.
Review recent changes to schedules, queue configuration, or job payloads.
known_resolutions: Restore worker or scheduler health if it is unavailable.
Correct the job failure after inspecting its error details.
Handle repeatedly failing messages according to the team's queue-recovery procedure.
